## Short bio

Justin S. Eloriaga is an Economist at the International Monetary Fund's Shanghai
Center (国际货币基金组织上海中心), the Fund's regional hub for the Asia-Pacific, which
promotes applied policy research on questions facing emerging market and
middle-income economies and serves as a venue for policy dialogue and knowledge
exchange across the region.

He holds a Ph.D. in Economics from Emory University, completed under the auspices of
the J. William Fulbright Scholarship. Before Emory he graduated summa cum laude with a
B.Sc. in Applied Economics and an M.Sc. in Economics from De La Salle University,
completing the ladderized degree in the fastest time recorded.

His research is in macroeconomics, with a focus on Bayesian time-series econometrics
and monetary economics. Recent work identifies Fed information shocks episode by
episode from the narrative record, replaces hard identifying restrictions with
narrative ones in oil-market and monetary VARs, and studies how monetary policy,
trade, and energy constraints propagate across Asia.

He is an Associate Editor at the *DLSU Business & Economics Review*. Before joining the
Fund he was a Visiting Instructor at Emory University's Department of Data and Decision
Sciences, an Assistant Professorial Lecturer at De La Salle University, and a Central
Bank Associate at the Bangko Sentral ng Pilipinas.
